messages:
elaine-sales: Heads-up: BankAlpha wants a Private deployment POC. Key asks: preserve client src IP for audit, single static egress IP for allowlists, and compatibility with their TLS-inspect appliance. They sent a compliance questionnaire (link). Can we spell out options and a minimal netops checklist?
kai-netops: TL;DR options: 1) PrivateLink + managed customer-side proxy (NAT+header signing) 2) VPC Peering/Transit for literal src IP 3) Dedicated connector appliance in-customer VPC. Each has tradeoffs for routing, ops, and security.
ravi-se: PrivateLink keeps customer changes small. If literal src IP is required we need routed peering and route exchange. Otherwise we can add an X-Orig-Src header at the proxy.
tara-arch: For the header approach, propose HMAC header signing: proxy adds X-Orig-Src and X-Orig-Src-Sig computed with a shared key. Our ingress verifies sig before writing to audit logs. This gives tamper-evidence without peering.
kai-netops: Note on SNI/TLS inspect: if their appliance terminates TLS and re-encrypts, function-calls that rely on client cert pinning or SNI-based routing might break. Need to confirm which features depend on unmodified TLS.
elaine-sales: They prefer network-layer src IP but said app-layer signed header is acceptable if tamper-evident and keys are rotated. Also asked about single egress IP costs vs plain PrivateLink.
sec-bot: Security note: E2E TLS to Redwood is preferred. If TLS inspection is used, customer must document key custody & rotation. Signed header approach acceptable if the signing keys are rotated and stored in KMS. No header may be used for authentication unless contractually agreed.
ravi-se: Quick checklist for customer netops (pasteable):
- Create an EC2/container in customer VPC to run egress proxy (recommended) or enable VPC peering routes
- Allow outbound to redwood-ingress ENI(s) on TCP/443 (or to public IPs if not using PrivateLink)
- Configure proxy to: add X-Orig-Src, compute X-Orig-Src-Sig (HMAC-SHA256), forward TLS to Redwood endpoint
- Open healthcheck port 8080 from Redwood healthcheck CIDR
- Ensure MTU 1500 or tune MSS (if tunnel/proxy used)
- Document TLS-inspect key handling and rotation cadence

tara-arch: Firewall allowlist sample (if using public egress):
- 198.51.100.45/32 TCP 443 (redwood-ingest-1)
- 198.51.100.46/32 TCP 443 (redwood-ingest-2)
- NTP/UDP 123 to company NTP
- DNS TCP/UDP 53 to company resolver
If using PrivateLink: allow traffic to interface ENIs and security-group-bind to proxy host.
kai-netops: Pricing note: managed connector/proxy in-customer VPC will be an add-on (monthly infra + egress). PrivateLink-only POC is cheaper in engineering time but may not meet literal src IP requirement. Tara will capture exact delta.
elaine-sales: Customer also asked if Redwood can attest header sig verification in writing for audit. Can we provide that?
tara-arch: We can provide an attestation statement: "Redwood verifies HMAC signature on X-Orig-Src and stores original header and verification result in immutable audit logs for POC duration." Legal/security to approve wording.
sec-bot: Attestation ok pending legal review. Include key rotation schedule and KMS usage in statement.
ravi-se: I'll draft the handoff doc: diagram, proxy container spec (image + env vars), sample iptables rules, and verification snippet (HMAC check pseudocode).
kai-netops: I'll produce MTU/TCP MSS caveats and small diagram showing PrivateLink + proxy path vs Peering path.
elaine-sales: Can we get a consolidated handoff by EOD tomorrow? Customer wants to begin connectivity tests Wed. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: Reminder: create ticket POC-901 and assign to eng-oncall for connectivity testing.
elaine-sales: Thanks team — I'll send the questionnaire and proposed plan after the handoff is ready.
